text:
devon: Heads up — scaling up Dedicated pool in us-west-2 is failing when we try to provision new GPU nodes. Lots of EC2 errors about SG rule throttling. Creating this thread to track and decide mitigation.
maria: Seeing the same. Provisioner logs show repeated 429s on CreateSecurityGroup/AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress calls, then EC2 instance creation times out.
cheng: Pasted a snippet from the autoscaler logs:

```
2026-10-12T15:22:10Z ERROR aws/ec2: RequestLimitExceeded: Rate exceeded for security-groups
status code: 429, request id: 9a1b2c3d
Failed to create instance i- -> rolling back
```

sarah: Is this the burst of SG creations when we spin up new worker ASGs? We create SGs per cluster/stack currently.
devon: Yes — our current flow creates a fresh SG per allocation group to scope port rules. That means hundreds of SG operations during a big scale-up.
maria: Quick workaround idea: reuse a shared SG for the Dedicated pools until we get quota increased. Less blast of SG API calls.
cheng: Agreed. Also AWS suggests batching rule changes and avoiding create/delete churn. We could pre-provision SGs per AZ and attach as needed.
\
deploy-bot: Incident created: IN-2026-1893 — EC2 SG rate limit affecting Dedicated pool onboarding. Notifying oncall.
aws-support: (via aws-support) We can increase EC2 security group API rate for account, but it requires a support case and justification. Best practice: reduce churn by reusing SGs and group rules. We'll link the case template.
maria: I'll open a support ticket now with the “API rate limit increase” template. Will include traffic patterns and a timeline for expected scale. Anyone have exact numbers we should include (peak SG create/sec)?
cheng: From the orchestrator metrics during the spike: ~120 SG create calls in 30s (4/sec) plus ~200 ingress updates. Also many retries — makes it worse. Put 10k instances as long term target, but immediate need is ~600 concurrent worker nodes across pools.
devon: For immediate deploys, I'm going to switch the provisioner to reuse `sg-dedicated-shared-1/2` for the pool and disable per-allocation SG creation. That should avoid new SG creates during the next rollout.
sarah: Please also add a flag so we can opt back to per-stack SGs if we need stricter isolation later. We'll document the tradeoff in the infra runbook.
maria: Support case submitted: CASE-78941234. AWS responded asking for region, account ID (redwood-prod-123), and example request IDs. I included the logs and the orchestration graph.
aws-support: We've escalated to EC2 team. They recommend (1) temporary reuse of SGs, (2) request increase for concurrent API calls, (3) consider using VPC security group rule objects rather than many distinct SGs for each stack. We'll reply with ETA in 24-48h.
devon: Patch merged to reuse SGs by default behind a feature flag: `infra.reuse_sg_for_dedicated=true`. Rolling to canary pool now.
cheng: Canary scaled OK — no SG 429s so far. Confirming instance launches succeeded in AZ-a and AZ-b.
maria: After we stabilize, let's follow up with a proposal: pre-provision N reusable SGs per-region/per-AZ and a lifecycle policy. That balances isolation and API limits.
sarah: Also add cost note: fewer SGs means fewer objects but not huge cost change; main benefit is reliability during scale.
devon: I'll keep CASE-78941234 linked in the incident and update when AWS responds. Thanks all for fast turnaround. :thumbsup:
maria: Postmortem action items:
- infra: default to reuse_sg flag for Dedicated scale-ups (devon)
- infra: add telemetry for SG op rate to alert at >10/sec sustained (cheng)
- infra: submit formal quota increase request if AWS requires (maria)
- runbook: document isolation tradeoffs (sarah)

cheng: Adding: consider caching security group IDs in the allocator to avoid repeated Describe/Create cycles.

aws-support: Follow-up: EC2 team provisionally increased API concurrency for account in us-west-2 for 72h while they evaluate. Please monitor and report any remaining throttles.
devon: Monitoring looks green. Closing immediate incident. We'll schedule the follow-ups for next sprint.
maria: Closing thread — will keep case open until quota is permanent. Thanks everyone.
